sections.heading: C — Driving the freeways
sections.markdown:
## C — Driving the freeways

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A78
Freeways are multi-lane, controlled-access, divided highways with no stops and no cross traffic, built for long trips with less fatigue and more safety. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A78
Safe freeway driving means keeping pace with traffic and staying alert, and vehicles moving slower than the normal flow must keep to the right. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A78
Weaving from lane to lane is dangerous; pick a lane moving at the pace you want and stay in it. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A78
When you must change lanes to pass or exit, check traffic carefully and signal well before you move. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A78
In a freeway breakdown, park completely off the traveled lanes and stay with the vehicle if you possibly can. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A78
The distress signals are an open trunk, a raised hood if weather allows, and a white cloth tied to a door handle or antenna, and an officer who sees them will help. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A78
Parking on the freeway is not allowed except in an emergency. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A78
To reach Alabama State Troopers about highway emergencies, crashes or drunk drivers, dial *HP, which is *47, free from a cell phone. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A78
Entrance ramps are short one-way ramps that lead to an acceleration lane, where you speed up to match through traffic if possible. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A78
From the acceleration lane, watch for a gap, signal, and merge smoothly into traffic. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A78
Freeway drivers should leave room for merging traffic, but an entering driver must yield if they do not. [A78]
Why it matters: the entering driver carries the duty to yield even when freeway drivers fail to make room.
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A78
Do not stop completely in the acceleration lane unless it is absolutely necessary. [A78]
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A79
On an entrance ramp with a YIELD sign and no acceleration lane, entering drivers obey the sign and stop if needed instead of forcing their way in. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A79
An interchange joins two highways at different levels with separate connecting roads, so vehicles can cross, enter or leave without interfering with others. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A79
Four common interchange types are directional, cloverleaf, diamond and trumpet. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A79
A directional interchange serves heavy traffic moving between only two legs, with other movements handled by ordinary diamond-type ramps. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A79
A cloverleaf interchange uses loop connections for turns on and off the freeway from four directions and removes left-turn and cross-traffic conflicts. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A80
A diamond interchange has four ramps for entering or leaving with the flow, and left turns are made after you leave the freeway. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A80
A trumpet interchange gives freeway access where another road meets it in a T, as a variation of the directional or diamond design. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A80
Plan your exit early and watch the signs, moving into the proper lane well ahead of time. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A80
To exit, signal, enter the deceleration lane and slow there, never slowing suddenly on the freeway itself, and be ready to yield or stop at the end of the ramp. [A80]
Why it matters: slow down in the deceleration lane, not in the through lane.
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A80
If you miss your exit, do not stop, back up or turn around; go on to the next exit and come back. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0080]

Glossary: freeway — a multi-lane, controlled-access, divided highway with no stops or cross traffic [A78]. Acceleration lane — the lane at the end of an entrance ramp for matching freeway speed [A78]. Interchange — a junction of two highways at different levels joined by connecting roads [A79].
Memory aid: speed up in the acceleration lane, slow down in the deceleration lane [A80].
